title: Árpád
fact_summary: The Hungarian prince named in the Byzantine chapter, elected in Etelköz and driven out with his people by the Pechenegs.

claims.text: The chapter says the Khazar khagan offered Levedi the title of prince; Levedi declined and proposed voivode Álmos or his son instead.

sources.locator: summary of DAI ch. 38 (exact page not fixed in the copy read)

claims.certainty_reason: Read only as Tóth summarises and quotes the chapter in Hungarian.

claims.text: It says Árpád was then installed as prince in Etelköz by being raised on a shield.

sources.locator: summary of DAI ch. 38 (exact page not fixed in the copy read)

claims.text: One passage says the Pechenegs fell upon the Turks and drove them out together with their prince, Árpád.
claims.certainty_reason: Read only as Tóth summarises and quotes the chapter in Hungarian.

claims.text: A 2022 genome study calls the 10th and 11th centuries the “early Árpádian Period”, after the ruling house.
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the study reports, read in the open copy linked under Sources.

claims.text: Using the two generations of leaders, Levedi and Árpád, the son of Álmos, the story told in chapter 38 belongs to the second half of the ninth century.
claims.certainty_reason: Argued by one tier B study.
